Ice sheets and glaciers exert a gravitational pull on ocean water. As ice melts, this pull weakens, causing water to redistribute away from the melting source.
*   **Near-Field Effect:** Regions *near* a major ice sheet (e.g., North America near Greenland; Europe/Africa near Antarctica) may experience **lower** sea level rise than the global mean. *   **Far-Field Effect:** Regions *far* from the melting ice sheet (e.g., the Pacific Ocean relative to Antarctica) will experience sea level rise **greater** than the global mean.
